data.long_meaning: Ayudhmat is the God of Weapons in Hindu mythology. The name Ayudhmat carries the meaning “God of Weapons” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayudhmat usually hope their child will grow to embody god of weapons and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayudhmat total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Ayudhmat is a significant deity in Hindu martial and war traditions. In Hindu epics such as the Mahabharata, Ayudhmat is revered as the divine, powerful source of all weapons. Warriors would invoke Ayudhmat before going into battle for victory and protection. Ayudhmat is also associated with the royal court and chariots, symbolizing power, strength, and righteousness.
data.spiritual_significance: Ayudhmat is believed to represent the sacred divine energy that bestows power, courage, and protection upon devotees. In Hinduism, weapons are metaphors for the spiritual power that transforms negative energies into positive ones. Therefore, Ayudhmat is also a symbol of inner strength, self-defense, and personal power. By invoking Ayudhmat, devotees seek to awaken their inner warrior and triumph over inner and external challenges. Ayudhmat is also considered as the guardian of relationships, particularly in the context of Dharma Rakshana (protection of duty and righteousness).
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ayudhmat signifies the divine protector or the one who holds the divine weapon. It is a name revered in Hinduism, representing the shield and strength that one seeks in the divine during times of need.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads, but a popular name for Lord Vishnu.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic containing 18 parvas or books. One of these books is the Udyoga Parva, in which the weapons of the Pandava heroes are blessed by the gods. Ayudhman is the name of the divine weapon of Bhima, one of the Pandavas.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is an Indian epic poem of Sanskrit origin, considered as the greatest work of Indian literature. It narrates the Kurukshetra war between two groups of cousins, the Pandava and Kaurava princes, over the throne of Hastinapura.

historical_references.reference: In the Puranas, Ayudhman is also known as 'Ayudhya' or 'Ayudhapati', the divine king of Haihayas (or Vahikas) in the city of Ayodhya. Ayudhman is considered the guardian deity of the city and a form of Lord Vishnu.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a collection of ancient Indian religious texts, containing mythology, philosophical insights, and historical records. They are considered essential sources of information for the Hindu religious traditions.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Sanskrit name 'Ayudhmat' is gaining popularity in modern contexts due to its association with technology, gaming, and culture. In the tech world, Ayudhmat is a character name from the popular strategy game 'Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition' by Microsoft Xbox. In the gaming industry, Ayudhmat is a playable character in the role-playing game 'Final Fantasy Tactics' by Square Enix. Lastly, in the cultural sphere, Ayudhmat is the name of the divine god of war and strength in Hindu mythology. These trends showcase the versatility and relevance of Ayudhmat in various fields, making it a fascinating name to explore.
